svg.aria-label: QBM-01 · Mitochondrial electron transport and oxidative phosphorylation
svg.text: QBM-01 · Mitochondrial electron transport and oxidative
phosphorylation
Magnetically addressable nodes of the plant respiratory chain, with the evidence tier for each shown as a border style

g.title: NADH / NAD+ tier T4 (verified) quantum class: structural_context
Succinate tier T4 (verified) quantum class: structural_context
O2 tier T4 (verified) quantum class: structural_context

Complex I (NADH:ubiquinone oxidoreductase) tier T3 (inferred) quantum class: flavin_semiquinone, iron_sulfur_4Fe4S, iron_sulfur_2Fe2S, ros_leak_site nuclei: 1H, 14N, 57Fe, 33S AGI: AT5G37510, AT5G08530, AT4G02580, AT5G11770 rationale: The FMN site forms a flavin semiquinone during turnover and is a known superoxide-producing leak site, and the Fe/S chain performs sequential one-electron transfers — both of the physical routes the radical-pair and hyperfine arguments require. No published experiment has applied a near-null field and measured plant complex I activity, so this is a hypothesis with a mechanism, not a result.
caveat: Electron transfer along the Fe/S chain is fast relative to plausible singlet-triplet mixing times, so a coherent radical-pair effect here is harder to argue than at the flavin. Treat the flavin and the cluster chain as separate hypotheses rather than one.

Complex I FMN site tier T3 (inferred) quantum class: flavin_semiquinone, radical_pair_acceptor, ros_leak_site nuclei: 1H, 14N AGI: AT5G08530 rationale: A one-electron-reduced flavin is the best-characterised magnetosensitive species in biology; the same chemistry underlies the cryptochrome radical-pair model. The review's argument is precisely that this chemistry is not confined to photoreceptors.

Complex II (succinate dehydrogenase) tier T3 (inferred) quantum class: flavin_semiquinone, iron_sulfur_2Fe2S, iron_sulfur_4Fe4S, iron_sulfur_3Fe4S, ros_leak_site nuclei: 1H, 14N, 57Fe, 33S AGI: AT5G66760, AT3G27380, AT5G40650, AT5G09600, AT2G46505 rationale: Carries all three cluster types plus a covalent flavin, and sits at the junction the review nominates as the bottleneck — a change here propagates into both TCA flux and respiratory electron flow.

Alternative NAD(P)H dehydrogenases (NDA/NDB) tier T3 (inferred) quantum class: flavin_semiquinone nuclei: 1H, 14N AGI: AT1G07180, AT2G29990, AT4G28220, AT4G05020, AT2G20800 rationale: FAD-dependent, so the same flavin semiquinone chemistry applies. Included mainly as the second confounder alongside AOX — a plant can route around a complex I lesion, which blunts any phenotype and must be controlled for.
Ubiquinone pool (UQ / UQH2) tier T4 (verified) quantum class: structural_context

Ubisemiquinone (UQ·−) tier T3 (inferred) quantum class: semiquinone_radical, radical_pair_donor, ros_leak_site nuclei: 1H rationale: A free-radical intermediate held in a protein pocket. If any respiratory species supports spin-correlated chemistry, this is the leading candidate.
Alternative oxidase (AOX) tier T4 (inferred) quantum class: structural_context AGI: AT3G22370, AT3G22360, AT3G27620, AT1G32350, AT5G64210

Rieske [2Fe-2S] centre (complex III) tier T3 (inferred) quantum class: rieske_2Fe2S, semiquinone_radical, ros_leak_site nuclei: 57Fe, 33S, 1H AGI: AT5G13430, AT5G13440 rationale: The Qo site generates a kinetically stabilised ubisemiquinone — a genuine, comparatively long-lived organic radical in a defined protein pocket, which is the most favourable setting for a field-dependent branching effect anywhere in the respiratory chain.
caveat: Qo-site semiquinone is short-lived and its occupancy is debated; a field effect here would be easier to argue if lifetime were measured under the relevant conditions.

Cytochrome c tier T3 (inferred) quantum class: heme_electron_carrier nuclei: 57Fe, 1H AGI: AT1G22840, AT4G10040 Racca2022: Cytochrome c and the transcription factor ABI4 link mitochondrial status to ABA-dependent seed germination. [10.1111/nph.18287] rationale: A one-electron heme carrier, paramagnetic in the ferric state. Included because Racca et al. place cytochrome c on the path from mitochondrial state to germination timing, which is the developmental window the review argues matters most.

Complex IV (cytochrome c oxidase) tier T3 (inferred) quantum class: heme_copper_binuclear, cu_a_binuclear, heme_electron_carrier nuclei: 57Fe, 1H rationale: The review names cytochrome oxidase explicitly as a candidate direct metabolic target. The heme a3/CuB centre passes through paramagnetic oxygen intermediates (P, F, oxoferryl) whose spin states are, in principle, field-addressable.
caveat: Strongly exchange-coupled metal centres relax very fast, which argues against coherent spin effects. This is a mechanistically attractive but physically demanding hypothesis, and is labelled T3 for that reason.
ATP synthase (complex V) tier T4 (inferred) quantum class: structural_context

Mitochondrial superoxide / H2O2 tier T2 (reported) quantum class: ros_leak_site AGI: AT3G10920 Parmagnani2022: Near-null magnetic field exposure alters ROS-associated transcriptomic and metabolomic programmes in Arabidopsis. [10.3390/biom12121824] Farooq2021: Reactive oxygen species and mitochondria jointly regulate seed germination, establishing the route from mitochondrial ROS to a developmental outcome. [10.3389/fpls.2021.781734] rationale: Not a magnetosensitive mechanism itself — it is the amplifier. A field effect too small to measure as a rate change can still register here, because ROS signalling is threshold-like.

Aconitase (ACO1/2/3) tier T3 (inferred) quantum class: iron_sulfur_4Fe4S nuclei: 57Fe, 33S AGI: AT4G35830, AT4G26970, AT2G05710 rationale: The review nominates aconitase as the sentinel of Fe/S integrity, and the biochemistry supports it: the exposed cluster iron makes aconitase the first TCA activity to fall under oxidative stress, so it reports cluster damage before anything else does.
caveat: Precisely because aconitase responds to any oxidative insult, a change under NNMF would NOT by itself implicate a magnetic mechanism. It is a sensitive readout and a poor discriminator; it needs a paired ROS-independent control.

Lipoyl synthase (LIP1) tier T3 (inferred) quantum class: iron_sulfur_4Fe4S, radical_pair_donor nuclei: 57Fe, 33S, 1H AGI: AT2G20860 rationale: A radical-SAM enzyme generating a 5'-deoxyadenosyl radical from a [4Fe-4S] cluster — genuine organic radical chemistry on an iron-sulfur centre, which is the tightest coupling of the review's two proposed mechanisms found anywhere in primary metabolism. Its product lipoylates pyruvate dehydrogenase and the 2-oxoglutarate dehydrogenase complex, so a defect propagates straight into TCA flux.
caveat: The radical is generated inside the active site and quenched within one turnover; whether a spin-correlated pair with a long enough lifetime to be field-sensitive ever forms is untested.

svg.text: The respiratory chain redrawn so that each node carries its quantum chemistry and the evidence behind it. Solid heavy borders mark
entities where a magnetic-field effect has been demonstrated (T1); solid light, where it has been shown for the containing process (T2);
dashed, where a physical route exists but no field measurement has been made (T3); hairline, structural context with no quantum claim
(T4). The map is almost entirely dashed, and that is the finding: the Arabidopsis near-null-field literature is developmental and nutritional,
and has not yet measured a respiratory complex directly. Alternative oxidase and the type II NAD(P)H dehydrogenases are drawn because
they are the confounders — a plant can route electrons around a lesion in complex I or complex IV, so respiration rate alone cannot test the
hypothesis and cytochrome-versus-alternative flux must be partitioned. Derived from: Figures 1A and 4 of Porterfield & Barker, "Plant
Responses to Near-Null Magnetic Fields" — expanded to gene level and bound to Arabidopsis loci. Node counts by evidence tier: T2=1,
T3=10, T4=6. Schematic topology only — no quantitative value is encoded in this base map; numbers appear only when measured data is
projected onto it. Values are the authors' published results from Parmagnani, Mannino & Maffei (2022), Biomolecules 12(12):1824
(doi:10.3390/biom12121824), not a reanalysis: NNMF-grown plants relative to GMF-grown controls. No raw data was deposited — the Data
Availability Statement reads “Data are available as supplementary tables and further data can be provided upon request”. Reported as fold
change; the authors treat a gene as regulated only outside their own thresholds of ≥2 and ≤0.5, which this page preserves rather than
re-thresholding. shoots, 7 timepoints (10 min, 1 h, 2 h, 4 h, 24 h, 48 h, 96 h). 2 of 10 identifier-bearing nodes received a series (20%); 7
nodes carry no gene identifier and cannot. multi-locus nodes aggregated by extreme at each timepoint. values were published as fold
change and converted to log2 for display; the reported SD is carried through the same transform. 1 node(s) reverse direction during the
course (AOX), which no single-contrast overlay can show. Each node is tinted by its most extreme timepoint and carries a sparkline of the
full trajectory: the colour says how far it moved, the line says when. A node with no measurement is left unfilled, which is not the same as a
measured zero.
